newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar vote may be this year - official source.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar vote may be this year - official source.

text.p: The run-off in Madagascar's presidential elections may be held by the end of the year, official sources told Reuters on Friday.

Sources at the High Constitutional Court (HCC) said December 29 was one likely date for the run-off between Didier Ratsiraka and Albert Zafy, the two ex-presidents who led 15 candidates in the first round of voting on Movember 3.
The HCC has yet to announce final results in the first round but provisional figures show retired Admiral Ratsiraka won 36 percent of the vote and Zafy, a professor of cardiology, got 23 percent.
The vote will be a replay of elections in 1993 when Zafy, riding a pro-democracy wave after two decades of authoritarian rule by Ratsiraka, beat the then military leader.
This year's elections were forced when the HCC upheld a parliamentary vote impeaching Zafy for repeated violations of the constitution.
